subject: C
topic: Means of Transport & Power Projects in J&K

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Jammu–Srinagar National Highway (NH-44) passes through which major tunnel that connects the Jammu region to the Kashmir Valley?
questions.explanation: The Jawahar Tunnel (also called Banihal Tunnel) on the old NH-44 route connects the Jammu region to the Kashmir Valley through the Banihal Pass. 'Chenani-Nashri Tunnel' is wrong because it is located between Udhampur and Ramban on NH-44 but does not connect to the Valley directly. 'Pir Panjal Tunnel' is wrong because it is the railway tunnel (not road) on the Banihal rail link. 'Zoji La Tunnel' is wrong because it connects Kashmir Valley to Ladakh, not Jammu to Kashmir.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Chenani-Nashri Tunnel:

(i) It is India's longest road tunnel on a national highway.
(ii) It is located on the Jammu–Srinagar National Highway.
(iii) It was inaugurated in 2017.
(iv) It connects Srinagar directly to the Ladakh region.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct. The Chenani-Nashri Tunnel (9.2 km) is India's longest road tunnel, located on NH-44 (Jammu–Srinagar Highway), and was inaugurated in April 2017. Statement (iv) is wrong because the tunnel connects Chenani (Udhampur district) to Nashri (Ramban district) — it does not connect to Ladakh.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Baglihar Dam (Baglihar Hydroelectric Power Project) is built on which river?
questions.explanation: The Baglihar Dam is built on the Chenab River in the Doda district of Jammu & Kashmir. 'Jhelum' is wrong because the major projects on Jhelum are Uri and Lower Jhelum. 'Tawi' is wrong because Tawi is a smaller river flowing through Jammu city with no major dam. 'Ravi' is wrong because Ravi flows mainly through Himachal Pradesh and Punjab.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Road transport is the most important means of transportation in Jammu & Kashmir.
Reason (R): The difficult mountainous terrain of J&K makes it challenging to develop extensive railway networks across the entire region.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — roads are the primary mode of transport in J&K connecting remote areas. Reason (R) is correct — the mountainous terrain with steep gradients and passes makes railway construction extremely difficult and expensive. (R) explains (A) because it is precisely the difficult terrain limiting railways that makes road transport the dominant means of connectivity.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following power projects with their locations in J&K:

Column I:
(a) Dulhasti Power Station
(b) Uri Hydroelectric Project
(c) Salal Hydroelectric Project
(d) Kishanganga Power Project

Column II:
(i) Baramulla district
(ii) Kishtwar district
(iii) Reasi district
(iv) Bandipora district

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Dulhasti Power Station is in Kishtwar district (ii) on the Chenab River. Uri Hydroelectric Project is in Baramulla district (i) on the Jhelum River. Salal Hydroelectric Project is in Reasi district (iii) on the Chenab River. Kishanganga Power Project is in Bandipora district (iv) on the Kishanganga River. The second option wrongly places Salal in Kishtwar. The third option wrongly places Uri in Bandipora. The fourth option wrongly places Dulhasti in Baramulla.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Udhampur–Srinagar–Baramulla Rail Link (USBRL) project is significant because:
options: It will connect the Kashmir Valley to the Indian railway network for the first time via an all-weather rail link
It is India's first underground railway project
It connects J&K directly to Pakistan through a cross-border rail link
It is the first solar-powered railway line in India
questions.correctAnswer: It will connect the Kashmir Valley to the Indian railway network for the first time via an all-weather rail link
questions.explanation: The USBRL project aims to provide the Kashmir Valley with its first all-weather rail connectivity to the rest of India. 'India's first underground railway project' is wrong because the project includes tunnels but is not an underground metro — and metro systems existed earlier. 'Cross-border rail link to Pakistan' is wrong because the project connects within India (Udhampur to Baramulla). 'First solar-powered railway line' is wrong because the USBRL is a conventional rail project, not solar-powered.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are major national highways passing through Jammu & Kashmir?

(i) NH-44 (Jammu–Srinagar Highway)
(ii) NH-1 (Srinagar–Leh Highway)
(iii) NH-144A (Mughal Road)
(iv) NH-48 (Mumbai–Pune Expressway)

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: NH-44 (Jammu–Srinagar), NH-1 (Srinagar–Leh), and NH-144A (Mughal Road connecting Shopian to Rajouri) all pass through J&K. NH-48 (iv) is wrong because it is the Mumbai–Pune route in Maharashtra and has nothing to do with J&K.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The installed capacity of the Uri-I Hydroelectric Power Project is approximately:
questions.explanation: Uri-I Hydroelectric Project on the Jhelum River in Baramulla has an installed capacity of 480 MW (4 units of 120 MW each). '390 MW' is wrong — this is close to the capacity of Dulhasti. '690 MW' is wrong — this exceeds Uri-I's capacity. '240 MW' is wrong — this is the capacity of Uri-II, not Uri-I.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about air transport in J&K:

(i) Srinagar's Sheikh ul-Alam International Airport is the main airport in the Kashmir Valley.
(ii) Jammu Airport (Satwari Airport) serves the Jammu region.
(iii) J&K has no operational airports.
(iv) Air transport plays a crucial role during winter when road connectivity is disrupted.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct. Srinagar has the Sheikh ul-Alam International Airport, Jammu has Satwari Airport, and air transport becomes critical during winter when Jammu–Srinagar highway is blocked by snow. Statement (iii) is clearly wrong as J&K has multiple operational airports.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Mughal Road is considered an alternative to the Jammu–Srinagar National Highway.
Reason (R): The Mughal Road connects Shopian in the Kashmir Valley to Rajouri in the Jammu region through the Pir Panjal range.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — the Mughal Road serves as an alternative when the main NH-44 is closed. Reason (R) is correct — it connects Shopian to Rajouri through the Pir Panjal range. (R) explains (A) because by providing another route between the Kashmir Valley and Jammu region through a different pass, it serves as an alternative to NH-44.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Salal Hydroelectric Power Project has an installed capacity of:
questions.explanation: The Salal Hydroelectric Project on the Chenab River in Reasi district has an installed capacity of 690 MW (6 units of 115 MW). '480 MW' is wrong — that is the capacity of Uri-I. '390 MW' is wrong — that is the capacity of Dulhasti. '900 MW' is wrong — that exceeds Salal's capacity.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are hydroelectric power projects located on the Chenab River in J&K?

(i) Salal Dam
(ii) Baglihar Dam
(iii) Dulhasti Power Station
(iv) Uri Power Project

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Salal Dam (i), Baglihar Dam (ii), and Dulhasti Power Station (iii) are all located on the Chenab River. Uri Power Project (iv) is wrong because it is located on the Jhelum River in Baramulla district, not on the Chenab.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Srinagar–Leh Highway (NH-1) remains closed during winter primarily due to:
options: Heavy snowfall at Zoji La Pass
questions.correctAnswer: Heavy snowfall at Zoji La Pass
questions.explanation: The Srinagar–Leh Highway passes through Zoji La Pass (at about 3,528 m) which receives heavy snowfall in winter, making the road impassable for several months. 'Flooding of the Indus River' is wrong because the highway is not affected by Indus flooding. 'Landslides caused by earthquakes' is wrong because the primary reason for winter closure is snow, not seismic activity. 'Construction of new tunnels' is wrong because tunnel construction does not cause seasonal closure.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The Chenani-Nashri Tunnel, approximately __________ km long, reduced travel time on the Jammu–Srinagar Highway by about two hours.
questions.explanation: The Chenani-Nashri Tunnel is approximately 9.2 km long, making it India's longest road tunnel. '6.5 km' is wrong — it underestimates the tunnel's length. '11.2 km' is wrong — it overestimates the length. '4.8 km' is wrong — it is less than half the actual length.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following means of transport with their significance in J&K:

Column I:
(a) Shikara
(b) Pony transport
(c) Ropeway/Gondola
(d) SRTC buses

Column II:
(i) Main public road transport in J&K towns and cities
(ii) Transport on Dal Lake and other water bodies
(iii) Used to reach high-altitude pilgrim sites and tourist spots
(iv) Gulmarg Gondola — used for reaching Kongdoori and Apharwat

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Shikara is the traditional boat used on Dal Lake and other water bodies (ii). Pony transport is used to reach high-altitude pilgrim sites like Amarnath and tourist spots like Thajiwas Glacier (iii). Ropeway/Gondola — the Gulmarg Gondola takes tourists to Kongdoori and Apharwat peaks (iv). SRTC (State Road Transport Corporation) buses are the main public road transport (i). The second option wrongly assigns shikara to ropeway. The third option wrongly assigns pony to gondola. The fourth option wrongly assigns shikara to pilgrim sites.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Dulhasti Power Station:

(i) It is located in Kishtwar district on the Chenab River.
(ii) Its installed capacity is 390 MW.
(iii) It is operated by NHPC Limited.
(iv) It is a thermal power plant using coal.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct. Dulhasti Power Station is in Kishtwar on the Chenab River, has 390 MW capacity (3 × 130 MW), and is operated by NHPC Limited. Statement (iv) is wrong because Dulhasti is a hydroelectric power station, not a thermal plant.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The first railway line in Jammu & Kashmir (Jammu–Udhampur section) was inaugurated in which year?
questions.explanation: The Jammu–Udhampur rail section (about 53 km) was inaugurated in April 2005, bringing rail connectivity to Udhampur. '2000' is wrong — construction was ongoing at that time. '2010' is wrong — by 2010 the Udhampur section was already operational for years. '1998' is wrong — the project was still under construction then.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Hydroelectric power is the primary source of electricity generation in J&K.
Reason (R): J&K has abundant river systems flowing through mountainous terrain with steep gradients, providing ideal conditions for hydropower generation.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — hydroelectric power is the dominant source of electricity in J&K. Reason (R) is correct — J&K has rivers like Chenab, Jhelum, and Indus flowing through mountains with steep drops. (R) explains (A) because the abundant rivers and steep terrain create the natural conditions that make hydropower the primary energy source.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Kishanganga Hydroelectric Project is built on which river?
questions.explanation: The Kishanganga Hydroelectric Project (330 MW) is built on the Kishanganga River (called Neelum in Pakistan) in Bandipora district. 'Chenab' is wrong because Salal, Baglihar, and Dulhasti are on the Chenab. 'Jhelum' is wrong because Uri and Lower Jhelum projects are on Jhelum. 'Tawi' is wrong because there is no major hydroelectric project on the Tawi river.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are traditional means of water transport in the Kashmir Valley?

(i) Shikara
(ii) Donga (houseboat)
(iii) Ferry service on the Jhelum
(iv) Submarine service

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Shikara (i), Donga/houseboat (ii), and ferry services on the Jhelum River (iii) are all traditional water transport modes in the Kashmir Valley. Submarine service (iv) is absurd — there are no submarine services in Kashmir's lakes or rivers.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Gulmarg Gondola is one of the highest cable cars in the world. Its second phase reaches which peak?
questions.explanation: The second phase of the Gulmarg Gondola takes passengers to near Apharwat Peak at about 3,979 m elevation. 'Kolahoi Peak' is wrong — it is the highest peak in the Kashmir Valley but has no gondola. 'Harmukh Peak' is wrong — it is near Ganderbal, not Gulmarg. 'Tatakuti Peak' is wrong — it is not connected by the Gulmarg Gondola.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Jammu–Baramulla railway line:

(i) It passes through the Pir Panjal Tunnel, India's longest railway tunnel.
(ii) The railway line connects Jammu to Baramulla in the Kashmir Valley.
(iii) The Banihal–Qazigund section was a key challenging section of this project.
(iv) The entire line was completed before the year 2000.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct. The line includes the 11.2 km Pir Panjal Railway Tunnel (India's longest railway tunnel), connects Jammu to Baramulla, and the Banihal–Qazigund section was the most challenging mountain section. Statement (iv) is wrong because the railway project is still being completed in stages; the Banihal–Qazigund section opened in 2013 and sections are still under construction.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The Pir Panjal Railway Tunnel, approximately __________ km long, is the longest railway tunnel in India.
questions.explanation: The Pir Panjal Railway Tunnel (also called Banihal Railway Tunnel) is approximately 11.2 km long, making it India's longest railway tunnel. '9.2 km' is wrong — that is the length of the Chenani-Nashri road tunnel. '8.5 km' is wrong — it underestimates the tunnel length. '14.5 km' is wrong — it significantly overestimates the length.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Pakal Dul Hydroelectric Project, one of the largest upcoming projects in J&K, is being built on which river?
questions.explanation: The Pakal Dul Dam (1,000 MW planned capacity) is being constructed on the Marusudar River, a tributary of the Chenab, in Kishtwar district. 'Jhelum' is wrong because major Jhelum projects are Uri and Lower Jhelum. 'Kishanganga' is wrong because the Kishanganga project already exists separately. 'Indus' is wrong because the Indus flows through Ladakh, not in the project area.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following tunnels with their primary purpose:

Column I:
(a) Jawahar Tunnel
(b) Chenani-Nashri Tunnel
(c) Pir Panjal Tunnel
(d) Zoji La Tunnel (under construction)

Column II:
(i) Railway tunnel connecting Banihal to Qazigund
(ii) Road tunnel to provide all-weather connectivity to Ladakh
(iii) Road tunnel connecting Chenani to Nashri on NH-44
(iv) Road tunnel at Banihal Pass on old NH-44 alignment

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Jawahar Tunnel is the road tunnel at Banihal Pass on the old NH-44 alignment (iv). Chenani-Nashri Tunnel is the road tunnel connecting Chenani to Nashri on NH-44 (iii). Pir Panjal Tunnel is the railway tunnel connecting Banihal to Qazigund (i). Zoji La Tunnel (under construction) will provide all-weather road connectivity to Ladakh (ii). The second option wrongly swaps Jawahar and Chenani-Nashri. The third option wrongly assigns Chenani-Nashri to railway. The fourth option wrongly assigns Jawahar to Ladakh.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The JKSRTC (Jammu & Kashmir State Road Transport Corporation) primarily provides:
options: Public bus transport services connecting towns and cities within J&K and to other states
Air taxi services within the Kashmir Valley
Railway operation and management in J&K
questions.correctAnswer: Public bus transport services connecting towns and cities within J&K and to other states
questions.explanation: JKSRTC operates public bus services within J&K and to cities in other states like Delhi and Chandigarh. 'Air taxi services' is wrong because JKSRTC is a road transport corporation. 'Railway operation' is wrong because railways are managed by Indian Railways, not JKSRTC. 'Shikara services' is wrong because shikaras are privately operated on Dal Lake.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about power projects and the Indus Waters Treaty:

(i) Under the treaty, India can use western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) for run-of-the-river hydroelectric projects.
(ii) India has unrestricted storage rights on the Chenab River.
(iii) The treaty was signed between India and Pakistan in 1960.
(iv) The World Bank mediated the Indus Waters Treaty.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (iii) and (iv) are correct. India can build run-of-the-river projects on western rivers, the treaty was signed in 1960, and the World Bank brokered it. Statement (ii) is wrong because India does NOT have unrestricted storage rights on the Chenab — the treaty limits India's storage capacity on western rivers.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Chenab Bridge (Anji Khad Bridge) on the USBRL project is notable because:
options: It is the world's highest railway bridge
It is the longest tunnel in India
It connects J&K to China by rail
It is India's first underwater bridge
questions.correctAnswer: It is the world's highest railway bridge
questions.explanation: The Chenab Bridge on the USBRL project, at a height of 359 metres above the river bed, is the world's highest railway bridge. 'Longest tunnel in India' is wrong — that distinction belongs to the Pir Panjal Railway Tunnel. 'Connects J&K to China' is wrong — the bridge is part of domestic connectivity. 'First underwater bridge' is wrong — it is an arch bridge over the Chenab River, not underwater.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Jammu–Srinagar Highway experiences frequent closures during the monsoon season.
Reason (R): The highway passes through landslide-prone areas in the Ramban and Banihal sections due to loose soil and steep mountain slopes.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — the Jammu–Srinagar Highway is frequently closed during monsoon due to landslides and road damage. Reason (R) is correct — the Ramban and Banihal sections have loose, unstable soil on steep slopes prone to landslides. (R) explains (A) because the landslide-prone geology is the direct cause of the monsoon closures.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Lower Jhelum Hydroelectric Project is located near which town in J&K?
questions.explanation: The Lower Jhelum Hydroelectric Project (105 MW) is located near Uri in Baramulla district on the Jhelum River. 'Kishtwar' is wrong — that district has Chenab-based projects like Dulhasti. 'Anantnag' is wrong — there is no major hydroelectric project there. 'Kathua' is wrong — it is in the plains of Jammu with no major hydro project.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following statements are correct about the Zoji La Tunnel project?

(i) It aims to provide all-weather connectivity between Srinagar and Leh.
(ii) It will reduce the distance and travel time on the Srinagar–Leh highway.
(iii) It is located at the Zoji La Pass in the Great Himalayan range.
(iv) It will be a railway tunnel for goods transport only.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct. The Zoji La Tunnel will provide all-weather road connectivity between Srinagar and Leh, reduce travel time, and is located at the Zoji La Pass. Statement (iv) is wrong because it is a road tunnel (not railway) and will carry all traffic including passenger vehicles, not just goods.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the installed capacity (in MW) of selected hydroelectric projects in J&K:

| Project | Capacity (MW) |
|---|---|
| Salal | 690 |
| Uri-I | 480 |
| Dulhasti | 390 |
| Kishanganga | 330 |

What is the total installed capacity of these four projects?
questions.explanation: Total = 690 + 480 + 390 + 330 = 1,890 MW. '1,560 MW' is wrong because it underestimates (perhaps omitting Kishanganga). '1,900 MW' is wrong — it is 10 MW more than the correct total. '2,100 MW' is wrong — it significantly overestimates the total.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Mughal Road historically connected which two regions?
options: Kashmir Valley to the Jammu region via Pir Panjal
Srinagar to Leh via Zoji La
Srinagar to Gilgit via Burzil Pass
questions.correctAnswer: Kashmir Valley to the Jammu region via Pir Panjal
questions.explanation: The Mughal Road was historically used by Mughal emperors to travel between the Kashmir Valley and the Jammu/Punjab region, crossing the Pir Panjal range. 'Srinagar to Leh via Zoji La' is wrong — that is the Srinagar–Leh Highway. 'Jammu to Pathankot via plains' is wrong — that is a plains route, not the Mughal Road. 'Srinagar to Gilgit via Burzil Pass' is wrong — that was a different historical route.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the impact of power projects on J&K's economy:

(i) Hydroelectric projects provide employment to local people during construction.
(ii) Power generation contributes revenue to the J&K exchequer.
(iii) Surplus power from J&K projects is sold to the national grid.
(iv) Power projects have no environmental concerns whatsoever.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct. Hydro projects provide jobs, generate revenue, and surplus power is sold to the national grid. Statement (iv) is wrong because all large dam projects have environmental concerns such as displacement, ecological impact on rivers, and changes to local habitats.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following transport routes with the regions they connect:

Column I:
(a) NH-44
(b) NH-1 (Srinagar–Leh)
(c) Mughal Road (NH-144A)
(d) Jammu–Poonch Road

Column II:
(i) Shopian to Rajouri
(ii) Srinagar to Kargil and Leh
(iii) Jammu to Srinagar via Banihal
(iv) Jammu to Poonch via Rajouri

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: NH-44 connects Jammu to Srinagar via Banihal (iii). NH-1 connects Srinagar to Kargil and Leh (ii). Mughal Road connects Shopian to Rajouri (i). Jammu–Poonch Road connects Jammu to Poonch via Rajouri (iv). The second option wrongly assigns NH-44 to the Leh route. The third option wrongly swaps NH-1 and Mughal Road. The fourth option wrongly assigns NH-44 to Poonch.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The installed capacity of the Kishanganga Hydroelectric Project is:
questions.explanation: The Kishanganga Hydroelectric Project in Bandipora district has an installed capacity of 330 MW (3 units of 110 MW). '480 MW' is wrong — that is the capacity of Uri-I. '240 MW' is wrong — that is the capacity of Uri-II. '690 MW' is wrong — that is the capacity of the Salal project.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the length of major tunnels in J&K:

| Tunnel | Length (km) | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Pir Panjal | 11.2 | Railway |
| Chenani-Nashri | 9.2 | Road |
| Jawahar Tunnel | 2.5 | Road |
| Zoji La (planned) | 14.2 | Road |

What is the difference in length between the longest planned tunnel and the shortest existing tunnel?
questions.explanation: The longest planned tunnel is Zoji La at 14.2 km and the shortest existing tunnel is Jawahar Tunnel at 2.5 km. Difference = 14.2 − 2.5 = 11.7 km. '5.0 km' is wrong — it calculates the difference between Zoji La and Chenani-Nashri. '9.2 km' is wrong — it is simply the length of Chenani-Nashri. '3.0 km' is wrong — it does not correspond to any correct calculation.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Which agency is primarily responsible for the construction of the USBRL (Udhampur–Srinagar–Baramulla Rail Link) project?
questions.explanation: The USBRL project is being executed by Northern Railways under Indian Railways as a national project. 'NHPC Limited' is wrong — NHPC handles hydroelectric power projects, not railways. 'Border Roads Organisation' is wrong — BRO builds strategic roads, not railways. 'JKSRTC' is wrong — it is a state road transport corporation operating buses.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the impact of transport development on J&K:

(i) Improved roads boost tourism in the Kashmir Valley and Ladakh.
(ii) Railway connectivity reduces dependence on weather-affected road transport.
(iii) Better transport promotes trade and movement of agricultural produce.
(iv) Transport development has no effect on employment generation.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct. Better roads boost tourism, railways reduce weather dependency, and transport enables trade. Statement (iv) is wrong because transport development creates significant employment — in construction, operation, maintenance, and related service sectors.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Uri-II Hydroelectric Project has an installed capacity of:
questions.explanation: Uri-II Hydroelectric Project on the Jhelum River has an installed capacity of 240 MW (4 units of 60 MW). '480 MW' is wrong — that is the capacity of Uri-I. '330 MW' is wrong — that is the capacity of the Kishanganga project. '690 MW' is wrong — that is the capacity of the Salal project.
